payloads.text:
I can’t honestly give **genome-personalized** training/diet recommendations yet, because GenomeClaw did not return your genomic data in this turn.

- `genomeclaw_status`, `genomeclaw_findings`, and `genomeclaw_pgs_list` all returned `error_type: network_error` with `raw_error: fetch failed`.
- The gene-panel calls returned `error_type: placeholder_rejected`; the tool reported it received a call-id string instead of a JSON object.
- A PRS compute attempt also returned `error_type: placeholder_rejected`.

**So the genome-specific answer is blocked.** I did, however, set up the right panel to retry: ACTN3/ACE/AMPD1/MSTN/COL5A1 for training; FTO/TCF7L2/APOE/LCT/CYP1A2/ADORA2A/ALDH2/FADS/HFE/GC/VDR for diet; and BMI/T2D/strength-related PRS audit.

**Provisional non-genome baseline until the service works:**

1. **Training for muscle/general fitness**
   - Lift 3–5 days/week.
   - Prioritize progressive overload on squat/hinge/push/pull/carry patterns.
   - Use mostly 5–12 rep work, with some 12–20 rep accessory work.
   - Take most working sets to ~1–3 reps in reserve.
   - Track volume and add load/reps gradually.
   - Don’t overfit to “power vs endurance gene” claims: ACTN3 has replicated associations with elite power/endurance status, but the literature does **not** support using it alone to prescribe training. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11014841/?utm_source=openai))

2. **Diet for gaining/maintaining muscle**
   - Protein: target roughly **1.4–2.0 g/kg/day**; higher may help during fat loss phases. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28642676/?utm_source=openai))
   - Calories: slight surplus if trying to gain muscle; maintenance/slight deficit if recomposition.
   - Creatine monohydrate is one of the better-supported supplements for strength/lean mass training. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28615996/?utm_source=openai))
   - Don’t assume FTO means “you need a special diet”: an individual-participant meta-analysis found no evidence that FTO genotype meaningfully changed weight-loss response to diet/lifestyle interventions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6168036/?utm_source=openai))
   - Caffeine personalization is worth checking once GenomeClaw works: CYP1A2/ADORA2A evidence is mixed for performance, stronger for anxiety/sleep sensitivity signals. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37844569/?utm_source=openai))

Once the GenomeClaw host is reachable, I can rerun the panel and turn this into a true personalized plan.
